page: Microsoft Azure E8-4as_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance within the Easv7 family, powered by an x86_64 AMD processor and hosted on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is configured with 4 dedicated vCPUs and 64.0 GB of system RAM, resulting in an allocation of 16.0 GB of memory per core. This high memory-to-vCPU ratio caters directly to software footprints requiring substantial memory allocations relative to computational core counts.

Hardware architecture for the E8-4as_v7 does not include integrated local disk storage, operating instead with support for Azure Premium Storage to fulfill persistent drive requirements. Additionally, the instance contains no specialized hardware accelerators or GPUs, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are provisioned directly with the server profile.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the constrained core architecture allows organizations running per-core licensed software to limit licensing expenses while maintaining access to a 64.0 GB memory capacity. This resource balance makes the E8-4as_v7 well aligned for database workloads, in-memory caches, analytics processing, and enterprise resource planning services that require dense memory without necessitating additional compute scaling.
